author: reek
body: Symbolic expression tree. The foundation of the entire math system. Every mathematical object -- numbers, variables, sums, products, powers, functions, matrices, sets -- is an Expr. Expressions are trees: a sum is a node with two child expressions. This is the Mathematica FullForm: everything is a head applied to arguments.

author: reek
body: Newton, not a scan: the guess halves the error each step, so this is logarithmic in n rather than linear. A discriminant can be large and a simplifier has no business walking to it one integer at a time.

author: reek
body: ExFn had no arm here, so two function applications always compared unequal -- and `simplify` below recurses until a step compares equal to its input, with no fuel. Any expression containing a function therefore never reached a fixed point and never returned. The chapter had never compiled, so this had never run.
